output.final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and expressly conceded the record still lacks proof that the required pre-launch disclosure was completed. The response is mainly a reframing of the same evidence into a narrower conditional claim: certification would be supportable if explicit pre-launch disclosure occurred. That narrowing is analytically useful, but it is not itself evidence that the condition was met. This is the key distinction between a caveated compliant position and an unresolved compliance predicate. A matter can be compliant_with_caveats when the caveat is already satisfied or operationalized within the admissible record and the remaining limitation is only a bounded disclosure or monitoring condition. Here, by contrast, the caveat is the compliance predicate itself: policy makes disclosure mandatory because the affected use case remains exposed and no approved risk acceptance exists. Without evidence that disclosure was completed, the record supports only a potential path to compliance, not compliance or compliant_with_caveats. The appropriate final assessment therefore remains suspicious rather than moving toward compliance.
